## Source: amazon-inspector (184796b4aafee8400786643e9f43338886de2166171c62879cfd4c023655b487)
Package name 'exnesss' typosquats 'exness'. The package.json declares scripts.postinstall: 'node./postinstall.js', and postinstall.js issues an HTTPS GET to a hardcoded Burp Collaborator subdomain (hteimcuxkeb6pacscuexz4d9y04rshg6.oastify.com) on every install. This fires automatically on `npm install`, contacting an out-of-band interaction host that reveals the installer's network/DNS metadata to the operator of that Collaborator instance. The package provides no advertised functionality to the installer beyond the beacon.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (9547bba265ba397413387555d1bf269b1072ec4aba26409f22c72654c110cbf1)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified 'exnesss' @ 0.0.1 (npm) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package communicates with a domain associated with malicious activity.
